result:
68 tests run, 3 failures — all three confirm real bugs in `CSVFormat`, matching its documented/expected behaviour. Everything else passes.

Bugs found (tests fail against current code, confirming the bug; the tests are correct per documentation/contract):

1. **`testEqualsShouldDistinguishTrimSetting`** — `CSVFormat.equals()` never compares the `trim` field, so `CSVFormat.DEFAULT` and `CSVFormat.DEFAULT.withTrim(true)` are reported equal despite behaving differently.
2. **`testEqualsShouldDistinguishAllowMissingColumnNames`** — `equals()` also never compares `allowMissingColumnNames` (nor `ignoreHeaderCase`, `trailingDelimiter`, `autoFlush`, `headerComments`), so formats that only differ in that setting are wrongly reported equal.
3. **`testWithRecordSeparatorRejectsInvalidValue`** — the javadoc for `withRecordSeparator(String)` states it throws `IllegalArgumentException` "if recordSeparator is none of CR, LF or CRLF", but the implementation performs no such validation and silently accepts any string.

All other 65 tests pass, covering construction/validation (`newFormat`, line-break checks, duplicate headers, quote/escape/comment-marker conflicts), predefined formats, getters' defensive copying, `withXxx` methods, `format`/`print`/`println`/`printRecord` output, `toString`, and serialization round-trip.
